# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

`modernc.org/gc/v3` — a Go compiler front end (scanner, parser, package loader, type checker) built as a standalone library. Work in progress: parsing is complete and heavily tested; the type checker is partially implemented (currently only the `builtin` universe package is checked in `NewConfig`; the full-package check call in `newPackage` is still commented out, see gc.go).

Everything is one Go package `gc` at the module root. This directory is the `v3` module inside the larger `gc` repository (v1 at the repo root, `v2/` alongside); work here stays in `v3/`.

## Commands

- `make editor` — the edit-cycle check: `gofmt -l -s -w *.go` then `go test -c -o /dev/null`. Code must be `gofmt -s` clean.
- `make test` — full suite: `go test -v -failfast -trctodo -exterr -heap`, then `git diff testdata/`. See "Golden files" below for why the diff matters.
- `go test -run TestParser -re '<regexp>'` — run one test on files whose paths match the regexp (`-re` also disables golden rewriting).
- `make test2` / `make parser2` — same but additionally walks `$HOME/src` as corpus (`-src`).
- `make race` — race-enabled run.
- `make back` — `-noback`: panic at the first parser backtrack (locates where backtracking is introduced).
- `make report` / `make nreport` — backtrack-frequency report per parser.go line / AST heap breakdown.
- `make benchmarks`, `make mem`, `make memgo` — benchmarks and alloc profiles (`BenchmarkGoParser`/`memgo` profile the stdlib baseline, not this code).
- `make build_all_targets` — compile-check every supported GOOS/GOARCH pair.
- `go generate` — regenerates `stringer.go` (Kind, ScopeKind, ChanDir, TypeCheck).

Useful test flags (registered in `all_test.go`): `-src <dir>` extra corpus to walk (default `.`), `-trc` print each file as processed, `-trctodo` print checker TODO errors to stderr, `-exterr` errors with Go source origins appended, `-heap` heap stats, `-noback`/`-panicback` panic on backtrack, `-trcee` log expected (skipped) errors.

## Architecture

**Full-fidelity AST is the core invariant.** A `Token` is 16 bytes (`source` pointer + token kind + index); all source text, including whitespace and comments, is retained as each token's "separator" (`Token.Sep()`). `TestParser` parses every `.go` file in the repo and in GOROOT and requires `ast.Source(true)` to reproduce the input byte-for-byte. Any parser or AST change that breaks round-tripping fails the suite.

**scanner.go** — hand-written scanner validated token-by-token against `go/scanner` over the whole corpus (`TestScanner`).

**parser.go** — recursive-descent PEG-style parser with backtracking:
- One `XxxNode` struct per grammar production, fields in grammar order, `List` fields for repetitions; all implement `Node` (`Position()`, `Source(full)`).
- Backtracking is bounded by a budget: `max(parserBudget /* 1e7 */, 16*len(src))`; exhaustion yields a "resources exhausted" error. Keep the budget proportional-to-source property intact for huge machine-generated files.
- The grammar uses `...PreBlock` production variants to resolve the composite-literal-vs-block ambiguity in `if`/`for`/`switch` headers.
- The parser also declares identifiers into `Scope`s (Universe/Package/File/Other) while parsing; each file gets its own package scope to allow parallel parsing, consolidated later by `Package.check`.
- This file was originally emitted by the generator in `internal/ebnf` but is now maintained **by hand** (no DO NOT EDIT header).

**gc.go** — the public API. `Config` (immutable after `NewConfig`; GOOS/GOARCH/GOROOT/GOPATH, build-tag evaluation, pluggable `fs.FS`, import-path lookup) and `Package` (`AST` maps file paths to per-file ASTs). `NewPackage` is concurrency-safe and deduplicates in-flight loads through the LRU 2Q `Cache` (`cacheItem.wait()`); cached entries are invalidated by file stat comparison. `NewConfig` loads and type-checks `builtin` to build the universe scope (plus `cmp` for Go ≥ 1.21).

**Type checker (WIP)** — `check.go` (`ctx`, `Package.check` → per-AST `check`), `type.go` (`Type` interface + `Kind`; type AST nodes double as `Type` implementations), `value.go` (constant evaluation via `go/constant`), `abi.go` (per-GOOS/GOARCH size/align/offset tables; regenerated by running `internal/abi.go` on each target platform). Checker error messages starting with `TODO` mark unimplemented paths (`-trctodo` surfaces them).

**internal/ebnf/** — standalone grammar laboratory (`package main`, own Makefile). `spec.ebnf` is the Go spec grammar; `peg.ebnf` is the PEG-adapted grammar. `make gen` there regenerates `internal/ebnf/parser.go` (machine-generated, DO NOT EDIT) from `peg.ebnf`; `peg.ebnf.fs`/`.cls` are generated FIRST/closure sets. Grammar experiments happen here; the production parser at the top level is edited directly.

## Testing conventions

- **Golden files**: `testdata/test_parser_<GOOS>_<GOARCH>.golden` etc. are sorted lists of files that parsed OK. Test runs overwrite them in place, so `git diff testdata/` after `make test` is the regression/progress signal — commit intended diffs, investigate unintended ones. Of the per-platform variants, only linux/amd64 is tracked.
- Files that stdlib `go/parser` also rejects, files with `// ERROR` annotations at the failing line, and entries in `notSupported`/`falseNegatives` (all_test.go) are skipped, not failed.
- `TestGoParser`, `TestGoNewPackage`, `TestGoTypeCheck` run the stdlib equivalents over the same corpus as baselines for memory/behavior comparison.
- `log`, `log-*` files in the tree are untracked scratch output of make targets — never commit them.
